subtitle: How a mortal king placed his crown at the feet of an immortal god

panels.shot: low-angle wide inside the dark sanctum, lit by oil lamps, with Marthanda Varma kneeling before the vast reclining form of Padmanabha
panels.action: Marthanda Varma, in royal attire but bare-headed, kneels with folded hands before the unseen idol of Sri Padmanabha in the lamplit sanctum of the ancient temple, his crown resting aside on the stone floor.

dialogue.text: In Thiruvananthapuram, a king who survived daggers and Dutch guns laid his crown before a stone god and declared, “This realm is Yours.” Why would a victor give away his own kingdom?

i18n.hi: तिरुवनंतपुरम में, खंजरों और डच तोपों से बचा राजा पत्थर के देव के आगे मुकुट रख बोला, “यह राज्‍य आपका है।” जीता हुआ राजा अपना राज क्यों छोड़ेगा?

panels.shot: sweeping bird’s-eye of Travancore’s hills, backwaters and coastline with a faint overlay of marching troops and trading ships
panels.action: A panoramic landscape of mid-18th century Travancore shows coconut-fringed coasts, inland hills and fortified outposts, with faint silhouettes of soldiers and merchants suggesting a kingdom forged by war and trade.

dialogue.text: By the late 1740s, Travancore had been hammered into shape by campaigns against feudal chiefs, Dutch forts and rival houses. A new state stood on the Arabian Sea, rich in pepper and promise.

i18n.hi: १७४० के आख़िर तक, त्रावणकोर जमींदारों, डच किलों और दुश्मन घरानों पर चढ़ाइयों से नए सिरे से गढ़ा गया। अरब सागर किनारे, कालीमिर्च और उम्मीदों से भरा नया राज खड़ा था।

panels.shot: medium close-up of Marthanda Varma in court, half in shadow, eyes distant, as nobles debate around him
panels.action: Marthanda Varma sits on a simple throne in a wooden-roofed hall, courtiers gesturing and whispering intensely while he leans slightly forward, his face composed yet tense, gaze turned inward.

dialogue.text: Marthanda Varma had crushed rebellious nobles and centralized power. Yet the memory of shifting alliances, assassins and fragile loyalties lingered. How long could one man’s will hold this machine together?

i18n.hi: मार्तंड वर्मा ने बाग़ी सरदारों को कुचला और सत्ता अपने हाथ में समेट ली। फिर भी साज़िशें, गद्दार और टूटती वफ़ादारियाँ याद से नहीं गईं। एक आदमी की मर्ज़ी से ये मशीन कब तक चलेगी?

panels.shot: slow push-in on a map spread on the floor with Marthanda Varma’s hand weighing down its edge, shadows of priests and ministers falling over it
panels.action: A palm-leaf map of Travancore lies unfolded on the polished floor, weighted by Marthanda Varma’s steady hand, as the faint silhouettes of a Brahmin priest and a minister loom at the edge of the frame.

dialogue.text: The king and his advisers saw the risk: a powerful crown could be seized, disputed, or broken. But what if sovereignty itself could be lifted beyond human reach?

i18n.hi: राजा और उसके मंत्रियों ने खतरा समझ लिया: इतना ताक़तवर ताज छिना जा सकता था, बाँटा जा सकता था, तोड़ा जा सकता था। पर अगर खुद सत्ता ही इंसानों की पहुँच से ऊपर कर दी जाए तो?

panels.shot: wide interior of the old Padmanabhaswamy Temple courtyard at dusk, devotees and brahmins moving through lamplight while Marthanda Varma stands at a distance watching
panels.action: In the stone courtyard of Padmanabhaswamy Temple, priests carry lamps and conch-shells as evening rituals begin, while Marthanda Varma stands near a pillar in plain white cloth, quietly observing the flow of worshippers.

dialogue.text: In Thiruvananthapuram, the ancient temple of Sri Padmanabhaswamy pulsed with ritual and memory. Here, Vishnu lay in eternal repose, believed to watch over kings and peasants alike.

i18n.hi: तिरुवनंतपुरम का प्राचीन श्री पद्मनाभस्वामी मंदिर, रीतियों और यादों से धड़कता था। यहीं विष्णु शाश्वत विश्राम में लेटे माने जाते थे, राजा और प्रजा दोनों पर नज़र रखते हुए।

panels.shot: close-up of Marthanda Varma’s face lit by a single oil lamp, eyes reflecting the idol within the sanctum
panels.action: A close view of Marthanda Varma’s calm yet intense face caught in the glow of an oil lamp, his eyes fixed on something ahead, tiny reflections suggesting the recumbent shape of the deity inside the sanctum.

dialogue.text: Temple records and later histories describe his devotion. For Marthanda Varma, Padmanabha was not just a symbol. He would be the unseen sovereign of a reordered realm.

i18n.hi: मंदिर के अभिलेख और बाद की कथाएँ उसके भक्ति भाव को दिखाती हैं। मार्तंड वर्मा के लिए पद्मनाभ सिर्फ निशान नहीं थे। वे नज़र न आने वाले, लेकिन असली सम्राट बनने वाले थे।

panels.shot: intimate medium shot inside a side chamber, Marthanda Varma consulting with a senior priest, both seated on the floor with palm-leaf bundles between them
panels.action: Marthanda Varma sits cross-legged on the floor of a small lamplit room, opposite an elderly Brahmin priest; between them lies a bundle of palm-leaf manuscripts tied with string, one leaf unrolled as they confer.

dialogue.text: Somewhere around 1749–1750, under the gaze of priests and scribes, a plan took shape. The king would perform Thrippadidanam, the ceremonial ‘placing at the sacred feet’ of his realm.

i18n.hi: १७४९–१७५० के आस‑पास, पुजारियों और लिखारियों की निगाह के नीचे एक योजना बनी। राजा ‘त्रिपादिदानम’ करेगा—अपना राज पवित्र चरणों में अर्पित करने की रस्म।

panels.shot: low-angle wide of the sanctum entrance at night, torches and lamps blazing, with royal guards and priests forming a corridor
panels.action: At night, the carved wooden doors of the sanctum stand open, the interior aglow with many lamps, as priests in white and royal guards with spears form a solemn corridor awaiting the king’s entry.

dialogue.text: The exact date and full sequence lie partly in temple records still guarded today. But all agree: one night, the sanctum became a court, and the stone deity a legal sovereign.

i18n.hi: सटीक तारीख और पूरी विधि आज भी बंद अभिलेखों में आधी छिपी है। पर सब मानते हैं: एक रात, गर्भगृह दरबार बना, और पत्थर का देव कानूनी मालिक।

panels.shot: epic low-angle inside the sanctum, showing only the outline of the reclining Padmanabha while Marthanda Varma kneels, crown and royal sword placed on a low step
panels.action: Within the dim sanctum, the massive outline of Padmanabha on the serpent couch looms in darkness as Marthanda Varma kneels bare-headed, offering a small crown and sheathed sword laid carefully on the stone steps before the idol.

dialogue.text: Kneeling before Padmanabha, Marthanda Varma is said to have dedicated himself, his kingdom and its treasury to the god. Thrippadidanam turned conquest into offering, and a throne into a votive gift.

i18n.hi: पद्मनाभ के सामने घुटने टेक, मार्तंड वर्मा ने खुद को, अपने राज और खज़ाने को देव को समर्पित किया माना जाता है। त्रिपादिदानम ने फ़तह को भेंट और सिंहासन को चढ़ावे में बदल दिया।

panels.shot: tight close-up on Marthanda Varma’s hands touching the stone floor in a gesture of surrender
panels.action: A close shot captures Marthanda Varma’s hands stretched forward, palms pressing the cool stone floor of the sanctum, fingers spread in a formal gesture of submission and reverence.

dialogue.speaker: marthanda_varma
dialogue.text: From this day, I am but Sri Padmanabha Dasa, servant of the Lord.

i18n.hi: आज से मैं सिर्फ़ श्री पद्मनाभ दास हूँ, प्रभु का सेवक।

panels.shot: medium shot of priests and scribes seated in a row outside the sanctum, writing on palm leaves while listening intently
panels.action: Outside the sanctum, a row of priests and temple scribes sit on the floor, one of them pressing a stylus into a palm leaf as they listen, recording the king’s declarations into the temple’s records.

dialogue.text: Temple records, later cited by royal histories and the Supreme Court, preserved this act. From then on, Travancore’s rulers styled themselves ‘Sri Padmanabha Dasa’—servants, not owners, of the state.

i18n.hi: मंदिर के दस्तावेज़, जिन्हें बाद में राजवृत्त और सुप्रीम कोर्ट ने भी माना, इस घटना को सँभाले रहे। तब से त्रावणकोर के राजा खुद को ‘श्री पद्मनाभ दास’—राज्य के मालिक नहीं, सेवक—कहने लगे।

panels.shot: wide shot of the palace audience hall where Marthanda Varma addresses nobles and officers, a large painting or emblem of Padmanabha behind him
panels.action: In the palace hall, nobles and officers stand in two lines as Marthanda Varma speaks from a simple platform; behind him, a large depiction of Padmanabha on the serpent couch dominates the backdrop.

dialogue.text: In court, this change was more than a title. Sovereignty was declared to rest in the deity. The king now ruled as vice-regent and administrator, accountable not just to men, but to a god who did not die.

i18n.hi: दरबार में यह बदला नाम से ज़्यादा था। ऐलान हुआ कि असली सत्ता खुद देव में निहित है। राजा अब केवल प्रतिनिधि और प्रशासक था—जवाबदेह सिर्फ़ लोगों से नहीं, उस अमर देव से भी जो मरता नहीं।

panels.shot: medium shot of Marthanda Varma seated at a writing desk, reviewing revenue records and temple accounts together
panels.action: Marthanda Varma sits at a low desk examining palm-leaf bundles, with one stack marked by a small idol of Padmanabha and another by a revenue tally stick, suggesting the link between temple and treasury.

dialogue.text: In practice, temple and state accounts intertwined. Land grants, revenues and offerings flowed to Padmanabha’s temple, even as the king used this sacred wealth to maintain armies, roads and a growing bureaucracy.

i18n.hi: हक़ीक़त में मंदिर और राज्य के खाते घुल गए। ज़मीन, लगान और भेंटें पद्मनाभ के मंदिर को बहती रहीं, और वही पवित्र दौलत सेना, सड़कों और बढ़ती नौकरशाही पर लगती रही।

panels.shot: low-angle shot of Marthanda Varma overseeing stone and wood works at the temple, scaffolding around the gopuram and artisans at work
panels.action: Marthanda Varma stands on a raised plinth near the temple, watching artisans and laborers working on scaffolding around the towering gopuram, stone blocks and carved wood scattered around the site.

dialogue.text: Under his patronage, the temple’s fabric and rituals gained new splendour—regular Murajapam recitations, ceremonial festivals and structural works around the shrine bound the people’s faith to the new state.

i18n.hi: उसकी छत्रछाया में मंदिर की इमारतें और रीतियाँ नए वैभव से भर उठीं—नियमित मुरजपम पाठ, भव्य त्योहार और गर्भगृह के चारों ओर निर्माण ने लोगों की आस्था को नए राज्य से बांध दिया।

panels.shot: slow push-in on a ritual procession circling the temple, with soldiers carrying torches alongside Brahmins and musicians
panels.action: A night procession circles the temple, Brahmin priests carrying lamps and conches while uniformed soldiers walk beside them with torches, drums and nagaswaram players leading the way through the crowd.

dialogue.text: Processions blurred the line between sacred and political. A deity’s palanquin and royal troops moved together, reminding villagers that the same unseen Padmanabha sanctified taxes, laws and war.

i18n.hi: जुलूसों ने पवित्र और सियासी के बीच की रेखा मिटा दी। देव की पालकी और शाही फ़ौज साथ चलती, गाँवों को याद दिलाती कि वही अदृश्य पद्मनाभ टैक्स, क़ानून और जंग को पवित्र कर रहा है।

panels.shot: medium shot of a peasant family and a local headman at a village shrine, listening to a temple messenger proclaiming the king as Padmanabha’s servant
panels.action: In a small village shrine, a temple messenger speaks with raised hand while a peasant family and a local headman listen; behind them, a simple image of Padmanabha hangs above an oil lamp.

dialogue.text: For villagers, news spread that the king himself was only a servant of the Lord. The idea carried comfort and caution: resisting the crown now meant resisting the god who owned the land.

i18n.hi: गाँवों में खबर फैली कि खुद राजा भी बस प्रभु का दास है। यह ख़बर सुकून भी थी, चेतावनी भी: अब ताज के ख़िलाफ़ उठना, उस देव के ख़िलाफ़ उठना था जो ज़मीन का मालिक है।

panels.shot: tight close-up of a modern-style historian’s hand turning a palm-leaf manuscript beside a printed book, both showing the term ‘Padmanabhadasa’
panels.action: A hand turns a fragile palm-leaf manuscript laid next to a modern printed book on Travancore, both showing the same stylised word illustrated as ‘Padmanabhadasa’ in their respective scripts.

dialogue.text: Modern scholars like K.N. Ganesh read Thrippadidanam as both devotion and design—a way to legitimize a post-feudal state and its sacred wealth by anchoring it in an immortal, uncontested sovereign.

i18n.hi: आधुनिक विद्वान, जैसे के. एन. गणेश, त्रिपादिदानम को भक्ति और राजनीतिक दाँव दोनों मानते हैं—पोस्ट‑जमींदारी राज्य और उसकी पवित्र दौलत को एक अमर, निर्विवाद मालिक से जोड़कर वैध बनाने की युक्ति।

panels.shot: wide shot jumping forward in time, showing a later Travancore ruler in similar pose before Padmanabha, echoing Marthanda Varma
panels.action: In a visual echo of earlier panels, a later Travancore ruler kneels before Padmanabha in the same sanctum, his posture mirroring Marthanda Varma’s, while attendants stand discreetly behind.

dialogue.text: Successors followed his path, continuing to rule as Padmanabha’s dasas. Over generations, this temple-state ideology outlived individual kings, giving Travancore a continuity that paperwork alone could not.

i18n.hi: उसके उत्तराधिकारियों ने भी यही राह पकड़ी, खुद को पद्मनाभ के दास कहकर राज करते रहे। पीढ़ियों में यह मंदिर‑राज्य की सोच, काग़ज़ी क़ानून से भी ऊँची स्थिरता त्रावणकोर को देती रही।

panels.shot: final contemplative close-up of Marthanda Varma’s discarded crown lying near the sanctum threshold as devotees walk past it unaware
panels.action: The royal crown rests near the worn stone threshold of the sanctum, slightly to one side, as the bare feet of anonymous devotees pass by in soft focus, the interior glow of the shrine beyond.

dialogue.text: In placing his crown at Padmanabha’s feet, Marthanda Varma turned a symbol into an institution. His act still asks us: when power is fragile, what stories—and which gods—do we make it answer to?

i18n.hi: मुकुट पद्मनाभ के चरणों में रखकर, मार्तंड वर्मा ने एक निशान को संस्था बना दिया। उसका वह कदम आज भी पूछता है: जब सत्ता नाज़ुक हो, तो हम उसे कौन‑सी कहानियों—और किन देवों—के आगे झुका कर टिकाते हैं?

title_i18n.en: Sri Padmanabha Dasa and the Temple State
title_i18n.hi: श्री पद्मनाभ दास और मंदिर राज्य

subtitle_i18n.en: How a mortal king placed his crown at the feet of an immortal god
subtitle_i18n.hi: कैसे एक नश्वर राजा ने अमर देव के चरणों पर मुकुट रख दिया
